about: Vocabulary of record for the Skill Heaven / Skill Hell line. A term is defined in exactly one lexicon file, ever; extensions (marketing-tasks/founder/lexicon.brand.json) ADD terms in their own namespace and may never redefine a core term. States: canonical (use this), banned (the oracle retired it — CI fails), parked (coined but unchosen — docs only, never user-facing copy or code), frozen (meant something specific once — archived docs only). A term is `banned` ONLY when founder/RATIFICATION.md already retired it; a term this repo is still arguing about is `parked`, never banned. Writing a linter is not a way to make a decision. AND: `canonical` is not inherited from an oracle citation. A word describing a surface that has not been built or demonstrated stays `parked` however firmly its backing entry is written -- otherwise the lexicon launders provisional decisions into enforced vocabulary, which is the drift it exists to stop, one level up.
namespace_note: THE LEXICON IS FEDERATED ACROSS TWO HQs. This repo owns core, gaia.research, gaia.brand, gaia.heaven and gaia.mcp; gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree owns gaia.skills and gaia.trust. skill-heaven and gaia-mcp own NO namespace — they consume. `gaia.registry` is rejected: the namespace is `gaia.skills` (same ruling as gaia-skill-tree#1258, "Gaia Registry" is not the product name). ONE TERM, ONE OWNER: a term is defined in exactly one file, ever. This root file carries the repo-wide config (scopes, exclusions, oracle path) AND the `core` namespace's own terms; every other owned namespace lives in a sibling founder/lexicon.<namespace>.json. Terms owned by the other HQ are mirrored NAME-ONLY into founder/lexicon.foreign.json so the gate can reject a redefinition without importing another repo's source.
scope_note: THE LEXICON IS LINE-SCOPED, NOT REPO-SCOPED. It governs the Skill Heaven / Skill Hell line only. This repo also hosts the craft lab, the context-diet lab, the Milim pet and unrelated reports, where `seed` is a PRNG seed and `budget` is a CI budget — different projects, different vocabularies, none of this gate's business. `docs/plans/` also holds Milim-pet, Live2D and asset plans, which are excluded by name for the same reason. Widening these globs to `app/**` or `content/**` produced 60+ findings against code that has nothing to do with postures; that was the gate over-reaching, not drift.

decisive.about: Docs that read as current guidance for the line: the oracle, live plans, the evidence matrix.

user-facing.about: Line copy a reader outside the project sees: the public story docs, the benchmark reports, the research pages.

code.about: Shipped source for the line. Parked vocabulary must never become an identifier.

terms.definition: Proposed oracle status: breaking it costs credibility, money, or another repo. Violating one is a bug, not a decision. Unratified — pends the oracle rewrite.
Proposed oracle status: the working answer, held until the build says otherwise. A failing test is sufficient to change it. Unratified — pends the oracle rewrite.
terms.note: Matched case-sensitively: the lowercase word is ordinary English and matched 184 innocent lines before this was scoped.
